domains.name: Employment & Wage Dispute
domains.framework: Payment of Wages Act 1936 & Industrial Disputes Act 1947
domains.explanation: This involves employment contracts, unpaid wages, delayed Full & Final (FnF) settlements, wrongful termination, or withholding of service certificates.
rights: Employees are entitled to timely disbursement of earned wages and statutory full & final dues.
Employers cannot unlawfully withhold relieving letters or accumulated Provident Fund (EPFO) benefits.
Unreasonable bond penalties that restrict trade or employment are generally invalid under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act.
actions: Gather appointment letter, employment contract, salary slips, and bank statements showing wage history.
Calculate the exact outstanding wage amount, notice period pay, and pending allowances.
Send a formal written legal demand email to HR, payroll, and management giving 7–15 days to resolve.
If unresolved, file a grievance on the Ministry of Labour portal (SAMADHAN) or approach the local Labour Commissioner.
documents: Bank Account Statement showing salary credits

authority.name: Ministry of Labour & Employment / State Labour Commissioner
authority.purpose: Official conciliation and statutory wage recovery forum.

domains.name: Consumer Protection & Defective Goods/Services
domains.explanation: This involves defective goods, deficient customer services, unfair trade practices, or refusal to honor warranties by sellers and service providers.
rights: Right to replacement, refund, or compensation for defective goods and sub-standard services.
Right against misleading advertisements, hidden charges, or prices exceeding Maximum Retail Price (MRP).
Right to register grievances online on the National Consumer Helpline and file electronic cases on e-Daakhil without a lawyer.
actions: Preserve purchase bill/tax invoice, order confirmation, and payment transaction receipts.
Take clear photos or unboxing videos documenting the defect or deficiency.
Submit a formal written grievance to the merchant's customer support and grievance officer.
Register a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (consumerhelpline.gov.in) or call 1915.

authority.name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH) & e-Daakhil Portal
authority.purpose: Consumer grievance redressal and Consumer Commission e-filing.

domains.name: Cybercrime, Online Fraud & Digital Extortion
domains.framework: Information Technology Act 2000 & Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
domains.explanation: This involves online financial fraud, unauthorized account access, non-consensual sharing or threats to leak private images, and digital blackmail.
rights: Right to privacy and criminal protection against blackmail, extortion, and non-consensual image dissemination.
Zero-liability protection for unauthorized banking transactions if reported to the bank within 3 days (RBI guidelines).
Right to immediate reporting on National Cybercrime Portal to freeze recipient bank/UPI accounts.
actions: DO NOT pay extortion money or delete evidence; preserve all chat logs, screenshots, and phone numbers.
Immediately report financial fraud by calling 1930 within the 'golden hour' or at cybercrime.gov.in.
Block compromised bank cards and notify your bank branch manager immediately.
For blackmail involving private photos, file a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in under the Women/Child or Cyber Harassment cell.
documents: Screenshots of Extortion Messages / Blackmail Chats
Bank Account Statement / UPI Transaction Ref
Phone numbers, Profile Links, or Email IDs of accused
Compromised APK / Link URL details (if applicable)

authority.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal & Cyber Police
authority.purpose: 24/7 National cybercrime helpline and financial fraud freezing.

domains.name: Education, College & Student Rights
domains.framework: UGC Notification on Verification of Documents & AICTE Regulations
domains.explanation: This involves educational disputes, unlawful retention of original educational certificates, admission fee refund refusals, or student harassment.
rights: UGC and AICTE regulations strictly prohibit institutions from retaining original academic certificates (10th/12th marksheets, degrees).
Students are entitled to proportional fee refunds upon cancellation of admission in accordance with UGC refund norms.
Institutions cannot hold documents hostage over disputed fees or penalty claims.
actions: Submit a formal written application to the Principal/Registrar demanding return of original certificates.
Cite the UGC Notification on Verification of Certificates (which prohibits document retention).
Lodge an online grievance on the UGC e-Samadhan portal (samadhan.ugc.ac.in).
If unresolved, escalate to the District Collector / Higher Education Directorate.
documents: Copy of Application requesting document return
Written refusal or communication from institution

authority.name: UGC e-Samadhan Portal / Ministry of Education
authority.purpose: Official student grievance redressal and regulatory enforcement.

domains.draftType: Formal Demand for Return of Educational Certificates

domains.name: Money Recovery, Unpaid Debt & Cheque Dishonour
domains.framework: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 & Civil Procedure Code (Summary Suits)
domains.explanation: This involves recovering unpaid loans, friendly debts, business dues, freelance payments, or dishonoured cheques.
rights: Dishonour of cheques due to insufficient funds is punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.
Creditors can file a Summary Suit (Order 37 CPC) for rapid debt recovery based on written acknowledgments or UPI proofs.
The statutory limitation period to initiate debt recovery is 3 years from the date of default or acknowledgment.
actions: Gather bank account statements, UPI payment receipts, WhatsApp chat admissions, or written promissory notes.
For bounced cheques, serve a statutory 30-day legal notice within 30 days of receiving the bank dishonour memo.
Send a formal written legal demand notice giving 15 days to refund the amount.
If unpaid, approach the Civil Court or District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for pre-litigation mediation.
documents: Bank Account Statement highlighting fund transfer
Cheque Copy & Bank Return Memo (if applicable)

authority.name: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) & Civil Court
authority.purpose: Pre-litigation mediation, legal aid, and recovery proceedings.

domains.draftType: Legal Demand Notice for Debt Recovery

domains.name: Tenancy, Rent & Security Deposit Dispute
domains.framework: Model Tenancy Act & State Rent Control Acts
domains.explanation: This involves rental agreements, unlawful security deposit deductions, arbitrary eviction threats, or disconnection of essential utilities.
rights: Landlords cannot withhold security deposits without presenting itemized repair bills for genuine damage beyond normal wear and tear.
Landlords cannot forcefully evict tenants or cut water/electricity utilities without formal judicial process.
Tenants are entitled to receipt of refunded deposit within the agreed notice timeline.
actions: Compile the signed rent agreement, deposit payment receipts, and handover inspection messages.
Send a formal written demand notice stating move-out date, inspection clearance, and refund deadline.
Give 7–15 days notice before seeking formal dispute resolution.
If unresolved, file a petition with the local Rent Tribunal or District Legal Services Authority.
documents: Security Deposit Payment Proof (UPI / Bank transfer)

authority.name: District Rent Authority / Legal Aid Clinic (DLSA)
authority.purpose: Tenancy dispute resolution and deposit recovery mediation.

domains.draftType: Security Deposit Refund Formal Demand Notice

domains.name: Police Conduct, Criminal Grievance & Zero FIR
domains.framework: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) & Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
domains.explanation: This involves police procedures, registration of FIRs for cognizable offences, citizen rights during detention, forgery, or police misconduct.
rights: Right to register a 'Zero FIR' at any police station across India regardless of crime jurisdiction.
Right to know grounds of arrest and immediately inform a family member/friend (Section 41B / BNSS § 36).
Women cannot be arrested between 6:00 PM and 6:00 AM without exceptional Judicial Magistrate orders.
Right to free legal representation at the police station under Article 39A.
actions: If a local police station refuses to file an FIR, send the written complaint via registered post or email to the Superintendent of Police (SP/DCP).
Obtain a stamped acknowledgment copy for every physical complaint submitted.
Approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free advocate assistance.
For police harassment, file a complaint with the State Police Complaints Authority.
documents: Written Complaint Copy with Date & Receiving Stamp
Identity Proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID / Driving License)
Names / Badge Numbers of police officers involved (if known)
Supporting CCTV / Video / Audio or Document Evidence

authority.name: District Legal Services Authority (NALSA) & SP Office
authority.purpose: Free legal aid, FIR escalation, and criminal justice assistance.

domains.draftType: Formal Criminal Complaint / Representation to SP

domains.name: Domestic Violence, Harassment & Safety Protection
domains.framework: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 & POSH Act 2013
domains.explanation: This involves domestic abuse, physical or emotional violence, marital disputes, stalking, workplace sexual harassment, or urgent safety concerns.
rights: Right to reside safely in the shared household and obtain immediate protection orders against violence.
Right to emergency shelter, medical aid, interim monetary maintenance, and child custody.
Right to 100% free legal aid and assistance through One Stop Centres (Sakhi) and DLSA.
actions: If you are in immediate physical danger, dial 112 or 1091 (Women Helpline) immediately.
Reach out to the nearest One Stop Centre (Sakhi Centre) or District Protection Officer.
Preserve medical reports, photos of injuries, and abusive messages in a safe, accessible location.
Contact the National Commission for Women (NCW) or State Women's Commission for urgent intervention.
documents: Audio / Video / Chat Records of Threats

authority.name: National Commission for Women (NCW) & One Stop Centres
authority.purpose: Emergency intervention, shelter, and legal guidance for women.

domains.draftType: Protection Application / Grievance to Women's Commission

domains.name: Property, Neighbour Dispute & Civic Grievance
domains.framework: Civil Procedure Code & Municipal Corporation Acts / Public Nuisance Provisions
domains.explanation: This involves neighbour disputes, obstruction of common pathways, property encroachment, noise nuisance, or municipal service failures.
rights: Right against unlawful obstruction of easementary access to one's property (Indian Easements Act).
Right against public nuisance and hazardous encroachments under civic municipal bylaws and BNSS § 152.
Right to register civic complaints with local municipal ward offices and Resident Welfare Associations.
actions: Take clear photos and video recordings of the obstruction or nuisance with date/time stamps.
Submit a polite written request or grievance to the Housing Society / RWA or neighbour.
If unresolved, file a formal complaint with the Municipal Ward Officer or local police station for public nuisance.
For persistent pathway obstruction, apply for a temporary injunction before the Civil Court.
documents: Photos / Videos of Obstruction or Damage
Copy of Written Communication / Notice to Neighbour

authority.name: Municipal Corporation Ward Office & District Legal Aid
authority.purpose: Civic nuisance removal and easement dispute mediation.

domains.draftType: Formal Grievance Notice regarding Property Obstruction / Nuisance

domains.name: Contract Breach & Commercial Dispute
domains.explanation: This involves failure to perform contractual obligations, breach of written or oral agreements, or non-delivery of agreed commercial terms.
rights: Right to enforce contractual terms or claim damages/compensation for losses incurred due to breach.
Right to issue a formal Notice of Breach requiring the defaulting party to cure the breach within a stipulated period.
Right to initiate commercial mediation or approach the Commercial Court / MSME Samadhaan (for registered entities).
actions: Review the signed agreement, highlighting key obligation clauses, payment milestones, and dispute resolution terms.
Prepare an itemized statement of losses or incomplete performance.
Send a formal Notice of Breach giving 15–30 days to rectify or fulfill obligations.
Explore pre-institution mediation at the District Legal Services Authority.
documents: Executed Contract / Signed Agreement / Purchase Order

authority.name: District Legal Services Authority / Commercial Court
authority.purpose: Commercial dispute mediation and civil enforcement.

domains.draftType: Legal Notice for Breach of Contract & Demand for Performance

domains.name: General Citizen Grievance & Legal Assessment
domains.framework: General Legal Principles & Citizen Welfare Statutes
domains.explanation: This is a general citizen inquiry or legal notice situation where initial facts need further clarification to determine specific statutory remedies.
rights: Right to understand any legal notice received before responding (never ignore a court or statutory notice).
Right to 100% free legal advice through NALSA & DLSA legal aid clinics under Article 39A of the Constitution.
Right to seek public information under the Right to Information Act 2005.
actions: Document a clear chronological timeline of events with all involved parties, dates, and locations.
Preserve all notices, letters, bills, SMS, emails, or physical records received.
Do not sign any document or make admissions under pressure before consulting a qualified legal advisor.
Visit your nearest District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) front office for free advice.
documents: Copy of Legal Notice or Letter Received (all pages)

authority.name: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) & DLSA
authority.purpose: Free legal counseling, notice interpretation, and legal representation.
